 With Martinelli and Cano, Fluminense name squad for year's biggest match 
 Go to the comments section Add to your bookmarks Share this article Fluminense announced their squad on Wednesday evening (21) for the decisive second leg of their 2026 Conmebol Libertadores semifinal against Palmeiras. The main news is the return of Martinelli and Germán Cano , who are among coach Marcão’s options for the match at Nubank Parque.
 The inclusion of both players stands out ahead of the Tricolor’s most important match of the season. Martinelli twisted his knee during the first leg and had to come off at halftime. Since then, the defensive midfielder had been working to recover in time for the decider and has now been named in the squad. Germán Cano is also available to the coaching staff again.
 OneFootball Videos
 The Tricolor go into the match trailing after losing the first leg of the semifinal. To reach the final without relying on penalties, the team must win by two or more goals. A one-goal victory would send the tie to a penalty shootout.
 Doubts and absentees 
 In attack, Canobbio and Kevin Serna are competing for a place in the lineup. Renê, meanwhile, returns after recovering from injury.
 Alisson, Matheus Reis and Riquelme are still working their way back to full training, while John Kennedy is out injured.
 Fluminense’s probable lineup is Fábio; Guga, Thiago Silva, Millán and Renê; Hércules (Martinelli), Nonato and Ganso (Lucho Acosta); Savarino, Canobbio (Serna) and Hulk.
 Trailing on aggregate, Fluminense need a decisive performance away from home to overcome Palmeiras and secure a place in the Libertadores final.
 The match kicks off at 9:30 p.m. at Nubank Parque in São Paulo.
